summary:
1. Prioritize Hindi scripts and native Devanagari titles as they consistently dominate both view counts (1,300+ views) and retention (66%+ stayed_pct). 
2. Open with the exact word 'सोचो' (Imagine) or pose a direct, counter-intuitive premise in the first sentence to bypass the initial swipe filter. 
3. Frame hooks around relatable physical comparisons (cars, dogs, everyday objects) rather than abstract scientific descriptions. 
4. Maintain concise narrative setups; avoid long explanatory preamble that drops stayed_pct below 40%. 
5. Target everyday curiosity traps like car mechanics, rain physics, and popular dinosaur misconceptions.
winning_hooks: जो car crash में पिचक जाती है, वो तुम्हें ज़्यादा बचाती है।
सोचो, तुम्हारे दांतों पर 3 छोटी cars एक के ऊपर एक रख दी जाएं। इतने ज़ोर से T. rex काटता था।
बारिश में गीली सड़क पर, तुम्हारी गाड़ी को रुकने के लिए कम से कम दोगुनी दूरी चाहिए।
avoid: English language titles and Hinglish transliterated hooks for mass-reach topics, as they suffer from terrible initial retention (dropping as low as 6.7% stayed_pct).
Academic or descriptive opening sentences like 'वैज्ञानिकों को ऐसी सूक्ष्म आकृतियां क्यों मिली हैं' which immediately trigger viewer swipe fatigue.
Complex multi-clause introductions that delay the core conflict or value proposition past the 2-second mark.
next_experiment: A/B test a newly formatted dinosaur topic: Video A uses the proven 'सोचो [Scenario]' hook structure in pure Hindi, while Video B uses a direct question hook ('क्या आप जानते हैं...') to see which format pushes stayed_pct above the 67% ceiling.
